messages:
marie: Quick heads-up — nsys trace from this morning (hosted load test) shows a new tail-latency hump after the kernel-selection tweak.
jonathan: ugh, details? which kernel and which path in the runtime? :thinking_face:
marie: matmul_fp16 got picked more often for long sequences. Hotspot is the dispatcher + memcpy around the kernel call, visible in the kernel timeline.
keerthi: do you have a timeline screenshot/trace id? can we repro locally with perfetto capture?
marie: trace id perf-1768604321 in the perf bucket. Key snippet from nsys: "cudaMemcpyAsync (-> device)" sandwiched between two NVTX ranges labeled `dispatch` and `kernel_exec` and the memcpy shows up very expensive.
dave: suspecting small-batch/large-batch mismatch: selector picks matmul_fp16 optimized for N=64 but we get N=16 frequently; kernel has warp underutilization -> more thread divergence and memcpy overhead.
anita: perf-bot posted a flamegraph: matmul_kernel_fp16: 43% total, memcpy 18%, dispatcher 12%.
marie: proposal: add tighter NVTX ranges: push a per-request span around the high-level inference request, then push a child range for `kernel:dispatch` and another for `kernel:exec:<shortname>` so perf viewers can collapse by span.
jonathan: +1. we should standardize a compact naming template so traces are searchable: suggest `r/<hash>/s/<span>/k/<kernel>`.
keerthi: two notes: 1) don't put raw request ids in traces (PII/size). We should hash and truncate: e.g., `r/h-9f2b/s/enc/k/matmul16_f16` 2) keep span names short to avoid perfetto UI truncation.
dave: agreed. also add metadata via NVTX attributes? perfetto supports color groups by `category` with `nvtxRangePushEx` on newer toolkits.
marie: example NVTX push/pop in C++ I used:
```
nvtxRangePushA("r/h-9f2b/s/dispatch/k/matmul16");
launch_kernel(...);
nvtxRangePop();
```
and Python context manager wrapper we can add to runtime bindings:
```
with nvtx.span(f"r/{hid}/s/{step}/k/{k_short}"):
    run_dispatch()
```
jonathan: can we add a note in the runtime to only enable per-request spans under a flag? default off for production traces, on for perf debugging.
anita: yes, add ENV var `REDWOOD_TRACE_SPANS=1` guarded. Also add sampling param `REDWOOD_TRACE_SAMPLE=0.01` to only tag 1% of requests.
keerthi: about the dispatcher hotspot: we should NVTX-range the dispatch internals (kernel-selection, layout-conversion, memcpy staging). That will let us see where time is spent per child step.
dave: got a repro plan: instrument dispatcher, run dedicated small-batch workload with `--sequence-distribution` skewed to 16, capture nsys with `--trace=cuda,osrt,ui` and perfetto protobuf export, then open in perfetto and filter by `k/matmul`.
marie: I'll push a small PR with the span helper + env flags and example traces attached. Also adding a quick README for the naming rules and hash guidance.
jonathan: tiny naming nit: use `k/` short kernel tag, `s/` for logical span (encode stage: alloc/dispatch/exec/post). Keep total path < 64 chars.
perf-bot: automated note — created perf run record perf-1768604321 (job 8927). Link: https://perf.internal/reports/8927
anita: thanks all. after we land spans let's rerun the canary and check if the dispatcher memcpy attribution shifts out of the kernel exec bar (means we misattributed before).
marie: exact next steps in PR: 1) add NVTX helpers + sampling 2) add docs/naming 3) instrument dispatch points 4) run controlled repro and attach traces. I'll ping when PR is ready. :rocket:
